title: Beyond the 956: Michael Giles, founding drummer of King Crimson, dies at 84
excerpt: Michael Giles, the founding drummer of the legendary progressive rock band King Crimson, died Monday, November 23, 2026. He was 84.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Michael Giles, the founding drummer of the legendary progressive rock band King Crimson, has died at 84.

Giles died on Monday, November 23, 2026, according to a statement from DGM Live, the record label founded by his former bandmate Robert Fripp. No cause of death was given.

"It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of Michael Giles, visionary drummer, composer and co-founder of King Crimson, who died on Monday 23rd November 2026, aged 84," the statement said.

Born on March 1, 1942, in Winton, Bournemouth, England, Giles began his musical career playing alongside his bassist brother, Peter Giles. In 1968, he co-founded King Crimson with Robert Fripp, Greg Lake, Ian McDonald and Peter Sinfield.

Giles played drums on the band's first two albums, including its landmark debut, In the Court of the Crimson King (1969) — one of the most influential albums in the history of progressive rock. His inventive, jazz-inflected drumming helped define the band's pioneering sound, and the statement from DGM Live credited his "rhythmic imagination, musical sensitivity, and inventive approach to drumming" as fundamental to King Crimson's music.

Giles is survived by his five children, Tina, Amanda, William, Rosie and Oliver, his grandchildren, his sister Marion and his brother Peter.

Sources: DGM Live (King Crimson statement); Consequence; Stereogum; Ultimate Classic Rock.
